newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran chief Ting had mild stroke - Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Ekran chief Ting had mild stroke - Mahathir.

text.p: Malaysian Ekran Bhd's executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing suffered a mild stroke recently, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday.

"I think he had a mild problem, but that is not something to worry about," Mahathir told a news conference after the signing of the engineering pact for the $5.5 billion Bakun Hydroelectric project, in which Ekran is the main promoter.
Asked if the problem was a mild stroke, Mahathir replied, "Yes, you can say it was a mild stroke."

Mahathir's comment follows days of speculation that the Ekran chief had taken ill. The rumours of his illness cropped up after the Bakun signing ceremony, originally scheduled for Monday, was postponed abruptly without explanation.
Fears that Ting was ill had also roiled the share prices of Ekran and other Ting-controlled companies on Monday.
Mahathir said on Tuesday that the delay in the signing was due to technical hitches.

Ting appeared at the Wednesday signing walking on his own steam and without visible signs of illness. Officials at Singapore's Mount Elizabeth Hospital earlier this week said Ting had been hospitalised for nine days this month and was discharged on Saturday.
"I am feeling very well, that is why I am here," Ting told reporters at a news conference following the dam construction signing ceremony. "Thank you very much for your concern about my health."

"The most important thing is this project has been signed. I will take it easy from now. The last three years I have been working, you people have been resting. Now I have finished my work, I have to rest," Ting added.
